# --format json emits the same report as a machine readable document, so a
# CI job can track the missed count over time or turn each miss into a
# ticket. It carries the mutated action's source and its replacement, which
# the text form leaves out.
#
# The byte exact assertion is on a dry run, because a real run records how
# long each mutant took and those numbers differ every time. A real run is
# checked line by line below.
#
# The golden file is named want.txt rather than want.json so that txtarfmt
# leaves it alone: it normalises embedded JSON to two space indentation,
# and the report is written with tabs.

muxt test-template-mutations --dry-run --format json --seed 1
cmp stdout want.txt

muxt test-template-mutations --format json --seed 1
stdout '"status": "KILL"'
stdout '"status": "MISS"'
stdout '"operator": "if-false"'
stdout '"seconds": [0-9]'
stdout '"killed": 2'
stdout '"missed": 1'

-- go.mod --
module server

go 1.24
-- templates.gohtml --
{{define "greeting"}}Hello, {{.Name}}!{{if .Loud}} !!!{{end}}{{end}}
-- template.go --
package server

import (
	"embed"
	"html/template"
	"io"
)

//go:embed *.gohtml
var templateFiles embed.FS

var templates = template.Must(template.ParseFS(templateFiles, "*.gohtml"))

type Greeting struct {
	Name string
	Loud bool
}

func Render(w io.Writer, greeting Greeting) error {
	return templates.ExecuteTemplate(w, "greeting", greeting)
}
-- render_test.go --
package server

import (
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

func TestGreeting(t *testing.T) {
	var buf strings.Builder
	if err := Render(&buf, Greeting{Name: "World"}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got, want := buf.String(), "Hello, World!"; got != want {
		t.Errorf("greeting = %q, want %q", got, want)
	}
}
